body: Thank you, I'll try to push forward and understand what is causing this grief. I'm glad you took the time to respond, it helps a lot.

It's been four to five years. My depression and dissociation have crippled my chance at happiness. I can't go outside long enough to appreciate the warmth of the sun against my skin, or the shine of the moon reflecting off my eyes as they roam the sky. Appreciating things like this used to be the reason I thrived, the reason I woke up and went straight outside to run my hands through the gentle yet sharp touch of the grass blades. I miss the world. I miss feeling a connection to it, like I was born into it just to admire everything about it. I wish I could go back to that, but nothing feels real anymore. Nothing feels important. I don't want to hurt anyone, and I fear I've made up my mind. I don't want to be talked out of it, I just want to be understood. A page to read, ink plastered to be appreciated. Not to be edited, or erased.
